A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexEvent research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching renamed components and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original FlexEvent detection results, frequency evaluations, component and hyperparameter ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds fusion-strategy comparisons in Figure 8 and additional DSEC-MOD measurements in Table 3.

M1.justification: FlexFuser becomes FlexFuse and FAL becomes FlexTune. The backbones, adaptive fusion, event sampling, losses, sparse-label training, temporal pseudo-label refinement, and self-training procedure remain equivalent. Section 3.3 reorganizes and illustrates existing steps.

E1.justification: Both use DSEC-Det, DSEC-Detection, and DSEC-MOD with the same object categories and frequency scenarios. DSEC-Det's car/pedestrian restriction and the empty-event evaluations already appear in v1's appendices; their increased discussion does not add coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially narrows DSEC-Detection's event-frame comparison from fourteen baselines to four, removing the attention and RGB-depth groups plus several fusion methods. Their presence on DSEC-MOD does not preserve those comparisons. Figure 8 adds Add, Concat, and Attention fusion controls. HDI-Former is newly mentioned, but no corresponding result is reported.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes DSEC-Det's stated split from test to validation while retaining its scores; this establishes a reported setting revision, not a rerun. Table 3 adds V.mAP and Avg columns without defining the F/V distinction. Main ablation averages now cover six rather than eight frequencies. The training budget and interpolation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 8 adds an ablation testing adaptive fusion against Add, Concat, and Attention at four frequencies. Some main-text qualitative examples are removed, while the complete appendix ablations and six appendix visualization sets are retained. Expanded Appendix C discussion does not establish additional experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds V.mAP and Avg results, including 25.2 and 36.9 for FlexEvent; its earlier 48.64 mAP becomes 48.6 F.mAP through rounding. Figure 8 adds fusion-control results, including 49.2 versus Attention's 40.1 at 180 Hz. Baseline rows and 27.5/30 Hz runtime entries are removed. Revised main-table averages reflect fewer frequencies; matched appendix ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The event representation, fusion equations, regularizer, training losses, and AP definition remain mathematically equivalent. Training losses previously numbered as Equations 8–9 are presented inline. No substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both retain the fusion-plus-frequency-adaptation contributions, early-work novelty positioning, superiority claims on the same three datasets, and robustness claims through 180 Hz. The introduction retains the same reported gains and performance-retention claim; renamed components do not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets sampling jitter as temporal augmentation against synchronization noise, explains the runtime implications of offline fine-tuning, and expands scene-specific interpretations in Appendix C. The sensor-quality, unseen-environment, and computational limitations in Appendix D remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly gives an approximate parameter breakdown of 1.5M for fusion and 44M for the backbone. It omits v1's exact inference CPU model/clock and the statement that DAGr training code was unavailable, without establishing changed availability. Training settings and the project and Appendix E resource links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to MoveEnet, HDI-Former, and Frame-Event Alignment and Fusion Network for High Frame Rate Tracking, and removes the Munir et al. reference associated with DRFuser. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning remain similar; publication updates to retained works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title and component names, regroups Section 3.3, condenses experimental discussion, expands Appendix C, and switches to numeric citations. The five-section main structure and Appendices A–E remain, with substantial prose carried over.

P2.justification: V2 adds the training illustration and fusion-ablation plot, redisplays existing appendix efficiency results in the main text, expands Table 3, and compresses several comparison and ablation tables. Main qualitative grids are reduced, and figures, tables, typography, and page layouts are extensively rearranged. Appendix visualization content is retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 8 addresses v1's lack of direct comparisons between fusion strategies, strengthening support for a central design choice, while Figure 4 clarifies the existing training procedure. These provide a modest gain in evidence and clarity. Narrower baseline coverage, undefined new DSEC-MOD metric labels, and unresolved split and HDI-Former reporting limit the improvement.
